chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (RA) said: al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban narrated from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Abu 'Umayr, from Jamil ibn Durraj, from Ibn al-Tayyar, from Abu 'Abd Allah (AS) who said:
Verily, Allah, the Mighty and High, will hold evidence against the people with what He gave them and made them to recognize.

key_terms.وَمَا عَرَّفَهُمْ: and what He made them recognize

ai.seo_question: What is the basis of God's argument against humanity according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Tawhid, Shaykh al-Saduq uses this hadith to establish the dual foundations of divine proof (hujjah): the innate intellectual faculties (aql) and the revealed guidance (naql). This underscores the Shia principle that accountability is based on the clarity of evidence provided through both internal reason and external revelation, ensuring justice in divine judgment.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 2. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (RA) said: al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban said, on the authority of al-Husayn ibn Sa`id, on the authority of Ibn Abu `Umayr, on the authority of Jamil ibn Durraj, on the authority of Ibn al-Tayyar that Abu `Abd Allah al-Sadiq (AS) said: “
Verily, Allah, the Mighty and High, will hold evidence against the people with what He gave them and made them to recognize.”
